decisions.quote: As expected for hand stimulation, our data showed an early modulation of MEPs, according to the congruency between the linguistically described actions and the stimulated effector. This early modulation is consistent with the data from the original study and supports the idea of an early involvement of the motor system in language processing. However, the direction of the effect is reversed with respect to Buccino et al. ( 2005 ), where an interference effect was shown.
decisions.location: Discussion, Experiment 1: TMS study (chunk_index 19, view_line_1based 22, original_char_offset 34950)
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly state that the early effector-congruent modulation of hand MEPs is consistent with the original study, whereas the direction of the effect was reversed (facilitation rather than interference) and the behavioral experiment's interaction did not replicate. Because the authors explicitly frame their findings as partly consistent with and partly contrasting with the original study without stating an overriding overall failure verdict, the outcome is mixed.
